title: 摸摸, 靓仔, morning, coffee or tea
subtitle: Chat with 老师, Nov 9–10, 2026
focus: 摸摸 · 靓仔 · 你累吗 · 还是

lines.en: To pat, stroke, or pet gently.
lines.note: 摸 mō (“to touch”) said twice. Doubling a verb like this makes it softer and more casual, so it comes across as “a little pat” or “give it a pet.” The second 摸 usually goes light and toneless, so it sounds like MŌ-mo. Common when petting an animal, or as a comforting pat on the head.
A common, cute use of 摸摸: a comforting pat on the head.

Slang from Cantonese (leng3 zai2), something like “good-looking dude” or “pretty boy.” Very common in Hong Kong and Guangdong; mainland internet slang picked it up too. People often use it playfully, even with strangers, the way you’d say “hey, handsome” or “hey bro.”
The female counterpart of 靓仔.
More common in Taiwan than 靓仔.
In messages, 你那边 often means “where you are” or “on your side.”
Use 还是 for “or” in questions. These questions already have 还是, so you don’t add 吗 at the end.

lines.py: Nǐ nà biān shì zǎo shang. Nǐ lèi ma?
lines.en: It's morning where you are. Are you tired?
lines.note: A more casual way to say it is 你那边是早上吧？累不累？ Here 吧 softens the guess, and 累不累 means “tired or not tired.”

lines.zh: 你那边是早上吧？累不累？
lines.py: Nǐ nà biān shì zǎo shang ba? Lèi bu lèi?
lines.note: A more casual version of 你那边是早上。你累吗？ 吧 softens the guess, and 累不累 means “tired or not tired.” 不 is often said lightly here: lèi bu lèi.

lines.zh: 台湾现在是早上。你累吗？
lines.py: Tái wān xiàn zài shì zǎo shang. Nǐ lèi ma?
lines.en: It's morning in Taiwan right now. Are you tired?
lines.note: If you're texting someone in Taiwan, they'll usually write it in traditional characters: 台灣現在是早上。你累嗎？
lines.trad: 臺灣現在是早上。你累嗎？

lines.py: Nǐ zài hē kā fēi hái shì chá?
lines.en: Are you drinking coffee or tea (right now)?
lines.note: 还是 already makes this a question, so you don't add 吗 at the end. In Taiwan's traditional characters: 你在喝咖啡還是茶？

lines.py: Nǐ xǐ huan kā fēi hái shì chá?
lines.en: Do you like coffee or tea?
lines.note: 还是 already makes this a question, so you don't add 吗 at the end. In Taiwan's traditional characters: 你喜歡咖啡還是茶？
